sections.html:
Every Iowa eviction begins with a brief written notice, and its length turns on why the landlord wants the tenant out. Under the Uniform Residential Landlord and Tenant Act, a missed rent payment draws three days, most lease breaches draw seven, and ending a tenancy with no cause takes longer.

SituationNotice the landlord must give
Unpaid rent3 days after written notice
Lease violation that can be fixedTermination not less than 7 days after receipt
Same violation again within 6 months7 days written notice, no fix period
Week-to-week tenancy10 days before the end date
Month-to-month tenancy30 days before the rental date

The unpaid rent rule is in section 562A.27(2), the lease violation rules in 562A.27(1), and the periodic tenancy rules in 562A.34. The nonpayment notice has to state the landlord's intent to terminate.

After the written notice, the tenant gets three days to pay all the rent. If it is not paid, the landlord may terminate. Section 562A.27(2) applies to rent that was unpaid when due, and the notice has to say the landlord means to end the lease.

One defense is available. A tenant contesting a nonpayment case has to prove every item here:

  • The landlord failed to meet the rental agreement or the repair duty in section 562A.15.
  • The tenant told the landlord at least seven days before the rent due date that they planned to fix the problem at the landlord's cost.
  • The repair cost no more than one month's rent.
  • The tenant made the repair in good faith before receiving the termination notice.

When the defense works, the repair cost comes off the rent claimed.

sections.h2: Notice to terminate versus notice to quit
sections.html:
The termination notice ends the lease; the notice to quit is the final warning before a lawsuit. Chapter 648 calls for a three-day written notice to quit before a landlord files a forcible entry and detainer case, which is Iowa's name for an eviction lawsuit.

A landlord who already served the three-day nonpayment notice and terminated under 562A.27(2) can file without a second three-day notice to quit (chapter 648).

A landlord can deliver it three ways: an adult resident signs an acknowledgment, someone hands it over in person, or it is posted on the main entrance and also sent by regular and certified mail. Mail service is complete four days after deposit, signed for or not. Service that skips these methods can leave the landlord without a valid notice.

sections.h2: How fast an Iowa eviction case moves
sections.html:
Quickly. The court sets the hearing within eight days of filing, or as late as fifteen days when the landlord asks for or accepts a later date.

Section 648.5 sets these timing rules:

  • The tenant must be served at least three days before the hearing.
  • If the hearing is set fewer than three days after service, the tenant must be told of the right to a continuance and gets one on request.
  • No default judgment can be entered without proper service.
  • If a genuine fact dispute exists, the court holds an evidentiary hearing and continues the case.

Skipping the hearing means losing by default, with removal ordered and no hearing on the merits. A written answer before trial is optional, and defenses and counterclaims can be raised at the hearing itself.

Judgment puts the landlord in possession. A tenant still in the house three days later faces an execution for removal.

The landlord then asks the clerk for a writ of possession and schedules the date with the county sheriff. The sheriff's office serves the writ, oversees the removal and returns the writ to the court. Removals must happen in daylight under section 648.20.

The loser has 20 days from judgment to appeal, but a tenant who lost must still move out while the appeal is pending. For a manufactured home in a community, either side can elect within three days to leave the home in place for up to 60 days, with utilities disconnected and no overnight occupancy between 7 p.m. and 7 a.m.

sections.h2: Can a landlord sue a tenant who stays after the lease ends?
sections.html:
Yes. Section 562A.34 allows a possession suit against a tenant who remains after the term without consent. A willful holdover in bad faith also exposes the tenant to actual damages and reasonable attorney fees.

For repeated rent or lease problems, section 562A.27(3) lets the landlord seek damages and an injunction, and attorney fees if the breach was willful. The tenant is excused only by showing due diligence and circumstances beyond their control.

One more limit applies. A landlord who knowingly lets the tenant stay peaceably for 30 days after the cause of action arises can be barred from the eviction proceeding under section 648.18. Delay can cost a landlord the case.

sections.h2: Where to get help with an eviction
sections.html:
Iowa Legal Aid runs six eviction help desks across the state. A tenant served with a hearing notice can start there.

County sheriffs carry out the final step but cannot give legal advice. Sheriffs recommend serving notices personally and having an attorney draft them, since requirements vary by the reason for the notice. Mobile home tenancies run on their own track, with a 14-day notice, separate from the notices in the table above.

Landlords should also call the sheriff ahead of the removal date if pets, vehicles, appliances, firearms or other dangerous items are likely to be inside. Planning for those items avoids delays on the day of the writ.

sections.h2: Selling an Iowa rental house during an eviction
sections.html:
An eviction in progress slows a listing and adds cost. Lender-backed buyers generally want a clean, empty house, and a court case or an occupied unit is hard to show.

Owners usually weigh three paths:

  • Complete the notice and court steps, then sell once the house is empty.
  • Sell with the tenant still living there and pass the lease to the buyer.
  • Agree on a move-out date with the tenant, then sell.

Cash Home Buyers purchases Iowa houses with tenants or damage and can talk through which path fits your dates. Whatever you choose, save every notice, the proof of delivery and any court papers. The title company and the buyer will ask for them.

Our Iowa landlord tenant guide covers deposits and the rest of the lease rules.

faqs.q: How many days does a landlord have to give for an eviction in Iowa?
faqs.a: It depends on the reason. Unpaid rent needs a three-day notice, a fixable lease violation needs a seven-day notice, and ending a month-to-month tenancy without cause needs 30 days.

faqs.q: Can an Iowa landlord evict without going to court?
faqs.a: No. After the notice period, the landlord must file a forcible entry and detainer action, win a judgment and have the sheriff carry out the writ. Removals happen only in daylight.

faqs.q: How long do tenants have to leave after a judgment in Iowa?
faqs.a: Three days. If the tenant has not left within three days of the judgment, an execution for removal issues. The loser has 20 days to appeal but must still move out.

faqs.q: What if a tenant repeats the same lease violation?
faqs.a: If substantially the same act or omission recurs within six months, the landlord may terminate on at least seven days' written notice, without a new chance to fix it.

faqs.q: Can I sell my Iowa house while the tenant is being evicted?
faqs.a: Yes, an owner can sell at any stage, but the open case and the occupant make a traditional sale harder. A direct sale to a cash buyer avoids showings and repairs.
